feature_request: create a server and client python files from which we can build a chat app so that two users can chat
acceptance_criteria: The server file initializes a socket to listen for incoming client connections.
The client file connects to the server via the specified host and port.
The application supports bidirectional text messaging between two connected users.
The server handles disconnection events gracefully to free up resources.
plan:
1. Define 'send_bytes' as a NEW FILE: chat_server.py. This file will implement a TCP server using Python's 'socket' and 'threading' modules. It will bind to 'localhost' on port 55555, listen for connections, and handle multiple clients concurrently using threads. Each client connection will be handled in a separate thread that reads messages and broadcasts them to all other connected clients, excluding the sender. It must gracefully handle client disconnections in a 'finally' block to close socket clients and remove them from the client list. 
2. Define 'send_bytes' as a NEW FILE: chat_client.py. This file will implement a TCP client using Python's 'socket' module. It will accept a 'username' and a 'host' (default 'localhost') and 'port' (default 55555) via command-line arguments or interactive input. It will connect to the server, send the username to identify itself, and then enter a loop to receive messages from the server and send messages typed by the user. It must handle disconnection gracefully, closing the socket upon exit.
